nodes.description: Post-HER XPS analysis and annealing recovery test
nodes.source_text: the as-prepared Oxi-1 sample showed a single peak attributing to lattice oxygen species at 529.8 eV. However, the Oxi-1 sample after the reaction exhibited two additional peaks at 531.3 and 533.4 eV... the reacted Oxi-1 sample was annealed... The results showed that the reactivity largely recovered to its original state.

nodes.description: EIS analysis at 175 mV overpotential - all catalysts
nodes.source_text: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was conducted at an overpotential of 175 mV... A small semicircle observed at high frequency was attributed to the electrochemical charge-transfer process... Another semicircle at low frequency... The time constant (τ₂) decreased with the oxidation degree of the catalysts
In particular, the Oxi-3 and Oxi-4 samples exhibited the highest reactivity and stability, respectively... the current decline in CV decreased with the increasing oxidation degree of the catalysts
This is further demonstrated by the chronoamperometry measurements shown in Figure S4f,g.
The capacitance of the Oxi-1 sample was similar to that of the Ni crystal with a value of 1.46 μF.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni single crystal exhibited no O 1s signal. Oxi catalysts show O 1s peak at 530.0 eV for lattice oxygen species increasing with oxidation degree.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results are shown in Figure 1b, where the Ni single crystal exhibited no O 1s signal. The O 1s peak at 530.0 eV, ascribing to the lattice oxygen species, gradually increased for the four oxidized model catalysts...

nodes.characterization_summary: STM image of fresh Ni single crystal revealed an atomically flat surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) image of the fresh Ni single crystal revealed an atomically flat surface (Figure 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM image shows many small nanoparticles of ~5 nm on Oxi-3 surface assigned to NiO species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) was employed to characterize the oxidation sample... As shown in Figure 1d, there were many small nanoparticles formed on the Oxi-3 surface with the size of around 5 nm, which could be assigned to NiO species.

nodes.characterization_summary: Oxi-3 surface exhibits O⁻, Ni⁻, and OH⁻ species with significantly higher concentration of surface oxygen species compared to Ni single crystal.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TOF-SIMS analysis was performed to identify the elemental species present on the Ni and Oxi-3 samples. As shown in Figure S2, the Oxi-3 surface exhibits the O⁻, Ni⁻, and OH⁻ species.

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical double-layer capacitance measured for ECSA estimation: Ni crystal 1.67 μF (ECSA 8.4 mm²), Oxi-1 1.46 μF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical surface area (ECSA) was measured in order to understand the intrinsic HER reactivity of electrocatalysts (Figure S5). The Ni crystal presented a capacity of 1.67 μF (Figure 3d), corresponding to the ECSA of around 8.4 mm².

nodes.characterization_summary: Oxi-3 shows highest HER reactivity with volcano relationship vs oxidation degree at 400 mV overpotential.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 3a, the Ni single crystal exhibited the lowest HER reactivity... the Oxi-3 sample showed the highest reactivity.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni single crystal Tafel slope of 136 mV/dec indicating Volmer step rate-determining; oxidized samples show 95-106 mV/dec.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3c presents the Tafel slopes of the electrocatalysts. The Ni single crystal displayed the highest Tafel slope of 136 mVdec⁻¹ which is approximate to the typical value of 120 mVdec⁻¹ indicating that the Volmer step was the rate-determining step.

nodes.characterization_summary: Time constant τ₂ decreases with oxidation degree, indicating faster water dissociation with more NiO species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The time constant (τ₂) decreased with the oxidation degree of the catalysts, suggesting that the water dissociation step proceeded faster with the increased generation of NiO species.

nodes.characterization_summary: Oxi-3 shows higher OH and adsorbed water species than Ni across H₂O pressures; residual OH persists on Oxi-3 after heating to >200°C while Ni desorbs completely.
nodes.evidence_snippet: However, as quantified in Figures 4e and S11, the OH and adsorbed water species on the Oxi-3 sample were found to be significantly higher than those on the Ni single crystal across various H₂O pressures.
